events.what: Greene and Lobb prove that Jordan curves formed by two graphs with Lipschitz constant < 1+sqrt(2) have an inscribed square, extending Tao's 2017 result
Ueoka self-publishes a claimed proof for all C0 Jordan curves (Zenodo, Medium), later stating on Zenodo that an error was found
events.credibility_reason: Author's own Zenodo note: 'An error was found in this proof, so we are considering an alternative approach.' Conceded, unfixed.
events.ai_basis: AI used for 'English drafting, translation, structured proof-checking, and detecting missing links in arguments, with Ueoka selecting and validating the final structure and mathematical content.'

events.what: Chambers, 'On the square peg problem' (close to C2 curves), journal publication 2025

judgement.doubts: Greene–Lobb's result is a new class of curves (a case), not a bound on a quantity; one could read the Lipschitz threshold as a bound, which would give progress, but the settled object is a restriction of the question so case fits. 'incident' is not an allowed ai_role; the Ueoka AI use (drafting/checking) would be none anyway, and the claim is knocked down. Chambers is pre-snapshot and only a partial result, so it does not make the problem open_stale.

outcome_prefix: Greene and Lobb (arXiv:2407.07798, 10 July 2024) proved an inscribed square exists for Jordan curves formed by two graphs with Lipschitz constant < 1+sqrt(2), a human-only case result.

corrections.why: F8/F6: the record chose the 'more eventful' Ueoka claim, which its own summary says the author conceded ('An error was found in this proof'); a knocked-down claim cannot set status, and the genuine advance in the record is Greene–Lobb.
F8/F1: Greene–Lobb settle a restriction of the bullet (a class of Jordan curves: two graphs with Lipschitz constant < 1+sqrt(2)), scope case → partial; Ueoka is discarded as knocked_down.

F8/F9: 'incident' is not a valid code; the status rests on Greene–Lobb, where the record says 'no AI involvement claimed anywhere in the paper'. Ueoka's quote in ai.basis_quote is left in place but belongs to a discarded event (and describes drafting/checking only).
other: a partial case proving squares exist for the curve class goes the way the conjecture predicts.
F8: credited humans follow the event the status rests on; record gives only surnames.
F6: the Zenodo claim is knocked down and no longer supports the status.
